section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "it is not wondrous nor distant" refers to the Torah and commandments both in their aspect of wonder and distance and in their essential state before descent, as all levels of Torah were given at Sinai.
section.t: And it can be said,
that this which it says "it is not wondrous for you nor is it distant,"
the intention in this is regarding the Torah and commandments as they are in the aspect of wonder and distance,
and also regarding the Torah and commandments as they are from their own essence
(before their descent,
when it is not applicable to say of them even the description of wonder and distance),
that even this level of Torah and commandments is not wondrous for you nor is it distant.
For at the giving of the Torah, all levels of Torah were given to Israel,
even the level of Torah as it is from its own essence
(before its descent to be relevant to the worlds),
and even to [the level of] "the Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He, are entirely one."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that according to the interpretation that this commandment refers to repentance, repentance in its essential state in the Master of Will is beyond the descriptions of wonder and distance, which only apply after its descent.
section.t: And likewise, according to the interpretation that this commandment refers to the matter of repentance,
that this [quality of] repentance being in the aspect of wonder and distance
is as it descended to be drawn downward,
but as it is from its own essence,
the descriptions of wonder and distance do not apply to it.
And although the wonder and distance of repentance are in a manner more elevated than the wonder and distance in all the commandments
[for the wonder and distance in all the commandments are the matter of Will and Wisdom
(as above in section 6),
and since repentance is in the Master of Will
(as above in section 4),
it is understood
that the wonder and distance of repentance are in a more elevated manner],
nevertheless,
since the description of wonder
(and certainly the description of distance),
even as it is in the ultimate elevation,
indicates that the wondrous thing has some connection to that which is wondrous relative to it,
therefore,
in the level of repentance as it is from its own essence
(the Master of Will),
it is not applicable to use the language of wonder and distance.
And that which is said that this commandment
(repentance)
is wondrous and distant,
it is
after its descent to be drawn downward.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the verse "it is not wondrous nor distant" refers to repentance both in its aspect of wonder and distance and in its root in the Master of Will beyond these descriptions, as it is from the level of "Anochi."
section.t: And it can be said,
that which is said "it is not wondrous for you nor is it distant,"
the intention in this is regarding repentance as it is in the aspect of wonder and distance, and also regarding repentance as it is from its root in the Master of Will
(which is above the description of wonder and distance),
that even this level of repentance is not wondrous for you nor is it distant.
And this is that which is said "for this commandment which I command you today,"
that even repentance as it is from the aspect of "Anochi,"
"I am that I am,"
is not wondrous for you nor is it distant.
